title: Ideal gas flow below Keplerian shear leaves a growing dust mode at corotation in a vertical field
abstract: We test whether differential gas rotation removes a dust instability at corotation. The same prescribed conducting gas sets linear drag and the ideal electric field. For a vertical field and a grain at rest on the synchronous ring, the planar determinant is a neutral phase root times a cubic. Its constant term is delta times (2Q - 3), where delta is positive stopping frequency in rotation units and Q is the gas angular-velocity shear. Signed charge and field cancel from this term. Every Q below 3/2 therefore has exactly one positive real root, for every finite field and charge. At Keplerian shear, some charge and drag values still give exponential growth. Other values give decaying transverse modes but retain a phase mode with linear drift. A cloud on nearby circular orbits then needs radial spread below 3.18e-4 of corotation radius to keep phase spread below 0.15 radians for 50 rotations. This is a conditional requirement, not a CPV measurement. We give the full transverse stability criterion, distinguish electric and drag shear, and check the result with symbolic algebra, 6,000 matrix tests and full-force orbits. The local test-grain model excludes gas response, nonideal fields and extra positional forces. It does not measure occurrence rates or lifetimes.
